evidence: Receiving DO2 online sensor: 3.64 mg/L at 48.0 h, 2.43 mg/L at 51.8 h (last observation)
Fitted decline slope -0.294 mg/L/h over 48.0-51.8 h; linear extrapolation reaches 0.34 mg/L by 60 h, below 2.0 mg/L within ~1-2 h under KEEP
Source batches held DO2 ~9-10 mg/L at the same age (e.g., source-1 ~9.3-10.0 mg/L, source-2 ~10.4 mg/L near t=48 h), isolating the defect to the receiving process
Receiving product assay 2.984 g/L at 47.8 h (available 51.8 h), still increasing, supporting continued production under reduced feed rather than a stop
Allowed action effects: strong_feed_reduction = feed x0.6, air x1.15 (max available DO relief short of stop)
args.rationale: Receiving DO2 crashed at t~48 h and is at 2.43 mg/L with a -0.29 mg/L/h trend; KEEP is centrally predicted to violate the 2.0 mg/L hard constraint within ~1-2 hours. increase_air (+15% transfer) and combined (feed x0.8) cannot be justified as feasible with the available evidence against a decline this steep, and no physics tool is provided to certify them. strong_feed_reduction (feed x0.6, air x1.15) provides the strongest oxygen-demand relief short of stop, retaining ongoing (though slower) product accumulation; stop is not necessary because a supported feasible operating plan exists.
args.uncertainty: No calibrated receiving-process model or physics tool is available; the effect of +15% aeration on the DO trajectory is unknown, so feasibility of weaker interventions (increase_air, combined) cannot be established. Feed-to-oxygen-uptake coupling is inferred from the observed DO crash and decline pattern. If the DO decline is transient, strong_feed_reduction over-corrects and sacrifices product growth rate unnecessarily; conversely, if demand keeps rising even this action may be marginal, in which case the next decision point should consider stop. The available extra assay is a product assay only and would not reduce DO uncertainty, so no measurement was requested.
